user.title: Add battery
user.description: Found {count} battery/batteries with a state of charge and a DC battery power sensor. Pick one, or choose the sensors yourself. Maximum {max} batteries.

specs.title: Factory data (other model)
specs.description: Enter the factory data of your battery. Defaults are those of the Marstek Venus E 5.12 kWh (90 % depth of discharge, > 6000 cycles, 80 % after 6000 cycles). Marstek gives no capacity guarantee in years.

data_description.nominal_kwh: Total capacity of the cells, e.g. 5.12 kWh.
data_description.reserve_kwh: Part of the nominal capacity the battery never releases. Datasheet: 90 % DoD, so 5.12 − 0.51 = 4.61 kWh = 100 % of new.
data_description.cycle_eol_pct: Manufacturer spec: e.g. 80 % after 6000 cycles (Marstek, Venus E Gen 3.0 product page). This is the spec line; not a warranty.
data_description.initial_cycles: Cycles before this monitor. Filled in from the battery's own total discharged counter when one is found (divided by the usable capacity). That counter measures on the AC side: an estimate, less exact than the cycles the monitor counts itself on the DC side. Without a counter: total discharged kWh so far ÷ usable capacity; leave 0 for a new battery.
data_description.red_pct: At or below this % remaining the status turns red: the moment to report it to Marstek via the Marstek app. Default 75 %.
data_description.tolerance_pct: Green while the measurement is at most this many points below the manufacturer spec line. Default 5.
data_description.purchase_date: The date the battery went into use. Warranty and age are counted from here.

details.title: Battery and sensors
details.description:
Check the proposal. The power sensor must measure the battery (DC) side, not the AC / grid side. Whether charging is positive or negative is detected automatically.

Optional: the highest and lowest cell voltage (cell balance check) and cell temperature (stored as context with every measurement). Filled in when found; leave empty if your battery does not provide them.

data_description.battery_id: Used in entity ids, e.g. mt1 gives sensor.marstek_mt1_capacity_pct. Lowercase letters, digits and _.
data_description.power_entity: Power measured on the battery (DC) side. W or kW.
data_description.cell_max_entity: Voltage of the highest cell, in V or mV. Only cell voltages, not temperatures.
data_description.cell_min_entity: Voltage of the lowest cell, in V or mV.
data_description.temp_max_entity: Stored with every measurement: a cold battery gives less. Only cell temperatures, not MOS / board temperatures.
data_description.temp_min_entity: Stored with every measurement: a cold battery gives less. Only cell temperatures, not MOS / board temperatures.

model.title: Which Marstek is {name}?
model.description:
Pick your model and the date it was installed. The factory data (capacity, depth of discharge, cycles) are filled in for you. You can change them later under Configure.

Venus C? It has 2.56 kWh, half a Venus E: pick Venus C, also when Venus E v1 / v2 is already selected.{counter}

packs.title: {model}: number of battery packs
packs.description: A {model} holds {kwh} kWh per pack. Rated capacity and reserve are calculated from the number of packs.

data_description.notify: A message on your phone (Home Assistant app) and under Settings → Repairs when the SOC meter drifts or the cells get out of balance, with advice. Only for a pattern: once is only recorded, 2× in 45 days is "attention", 3× is advice. Off = no messages; the card still shows it.
data_description.sidebar: Battery capacity in the sidebar, with all your batteries in it. Applies to the whole menu item: off for one battery = no menu item.
data_description.soc_sensitivity: When a deviation of the SOC meter counts. Normal: 5 % or more. Relaxed: 8 %. Strict: 3 %. Off: only shown on the card, never "attention" or advice.
data_description.cell_sensitivity: When the cell spread counts as too high. Normal: 2× the own normal value. Relaxed: 3×. Strict: 1.5×. Off: only shown on the card. Only with cell voltage sensors.

check_model.title: {name}: is the model right?
check_model.description:
The measured capacity is {pct} % of new: about half of the {kwh} kWh that is set. That usually means a wrong model, not a worn battery. A Venus C has 2.56 kWh, half a Venus E.

Is it a Venus C? Under Settings → Devices & services → Marstek Capacity Monitor → Configure, set the rated capacity to 2.56 kWh and the reserve to 0.26 kWh. The measurements are then recalculated.

Is the model right? Then report it via the Marstek app.

This message disappears by itself when the measurement is no longer about half.
